title: Het, die, dat, er
subtitle: Small words, big rules
intro: By the end of this lesson you can choose between het, die and dat without stopping to think. You will also recognise the four main jobs of er, and you will know when Dutch points back at a thing with die and when with het.

words.note: A small word with several jobs: 'there', 'of them', and a partner for prepositions.
Points to a place further away; hier is 'here'.
Only with de-words and plurals; het-words take dit.
Only with het-words: dit huis, dit boek.
Also a relative pronoun: de man die daar woont.
Also relative: het boek dat ik lees.
er + over; used for things, not people.
er + met.
er + van.
er + in.
In questions: Is er iets?
Already negative: don't add niet ('Ik heb niets').

example.nl: Er is iemand aan de deur.
example.en: There is someone at the door.

words.note: Alles is always singular: Alles is klaar.
One word, always singular: Iedereen is er.
Always before a plural noun: sommige mensen.

example.en: I have a lot of work.

words.note: Opposite of weinig; also te veel = too much.
It can go before or after the noun: genoeg geld / geld genoeg.
For exactly two: allebei de dozen.
A little more formal than allebei.
Use elke before de-words: elke dag.
Use iedere before de-words: iedere dag.

phrases.note: Existential er: er is / er zijn.
After a number, er means 'of them'.

grammar.title: Deze of dit? Die of dat?
grammar.explanation: **Deze** and **die** go with de-words and plurals. **Dit** and **dat** go with het-words. The same words also work as relative pronouns: **die** for de-words and plurals, **dat** for het-words. In a relative clause the verb goes to the end.

examples.nl: Het pakket dat ik heb besteld, is er niet.
examples.en: The parcel that I ordered isn't here.

grammar.tip: Ask yourself: de or het? De -> deze/die, het -> dit/dat.

grammar.title: Er: klein woord, vier taken
grammar.explanation: **Er** has four jobs. It says that something exists (**Er is**, **Er zijn**), it means 'there' as a place, it means 'of them' after a number, and it joins a preposition to point back at a thing: **erover**, **ermee**, **ervan**, **erin**.

examples.nl: Er staan nog drie dozen in de keuken.
examples.en: There are still three boxes in the kitchen.

grammar.tip: Er + preposition is written as one word: over -> erover, met -> ermee, van -> ervan, in -> erin.

grammar.title: Naar dingen wijzen: die of het
grammar.explanation: When you talk about a thing you already mentioned, use **die** (or **hij**) for de-words and **het** for het-words. For plurals use **die** or **ze**.

examples.nl: Waar is de sleutel? Die ligt op tafel.
examples.en: Where's the key? It's on the table.

examples.nl: Waar is het pakket? Het ligt bij de deur.
examples.en: Where's the parcel? It's by the door.

grammar.tip: Never use het for a de-word: 'Waar is de sleutel?' - 'Die ligt daar', not 'Het ligt daar'.

dialogue.title: De verhuizing
dialogue.setting: Youssef helps Sanne move into a new apartment in Utrecht.

lines.speaker: Youssef
lines.nl: Zo, is alles al in de dozen?
lines.en: So, is everything already in the boxes?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Nog niet. Er staan nog drie in de keuken.
lines.en: Not yet. There are still three in the kitchen.

lines.speaker: Youssef
lines.nl: En die grote doos bij de deur? Wat zit erin?
lines.en: And that big box by the door? What's in it?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Boeken. Ik heb er te veel.
lines.en: Books. I have too many of them.

lines.speaker: Youssef
lines.nl: Ik neem er twee mee naar de auto.
lines.en: I'll take two of them to the car.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Dank je. Deze doos is voor jou. Hij is wel groot.
lines.en: Thanks. This box is for you. It is big, though.

lines.speaker: Youssef
lines.nl: Geen probleem, ik ben sterk. Wat zit erin?
lines.en: No problem, I'm strong. What's in it?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: De pannen. En iets voor jou.
lines.en: The pans. And something for you.

lines.speaker: Youssef
lines.nl: Voor mij? Dat is aardig! Wat is het?
lines.en: For me? That's kind! What is it?

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Dat zie je straks. Niemand weet het nog.
lines.en: You'll see later. Nobody knows yet.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Allebei mijn ouders komen, en sommige vrienden.
lines.en: Both my parents are coming, and some friends.

lines.speaker: Sanne
lines.nl: Die is daar, naast de trap.
lines.en: It's there, next to the stairs.

exercises.explain: 'Het huis' is a het-word, so use dit (and dat).
Plurals take deze and die, never dit or dat.
After a number, er means 'of them'.

exercises.nl: Waar is de sleutel? ___ ligt op tafel.
exercises.explain: 'De sleutel' is a de-word, so use die (or hij).
After a number, er means 'of them': 'Ik heb er twee.'
Use 'er is' for one thing and 'er zijn' for more: 'Er is een probleem.'
'ermee' is one word and goes before 'bezig': 'Ik ben ermee bezig.'
With 'nadenken over', the thing becomes 'erover': 'Ik denk erover na.'

exercises.text: Er ___ veel dozen in de kamer.
exercises.en: There are many boxes in the room.
exercises.explain: For more than one thing use 'er zijn'; for things standing or lying you can also use 'er staan' or 'er liggen': 'Er staan veel dozen in de kamer.'
'Everyone' is 'iedereen' and takes a singular verb: 'Is iedereen er?'

exercises.focus: existential er: er is / er zijn

mistakes.pattern: Translates 'there are' with 'Het zijn' (Het zijn twee dozen).
mistakes.explain: Use 'er' for 'there are': 'Er zijn twee dozen.' 'Het zijn...' means 'They are...'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'is' with plural 'dozen' (Er is twee dozen).
mistakes.explain: With a plural subject use 'zijn': 'Er zijn twee dozen.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves the plural unmarked after 'twee' (Er zijn twee doos / twee doze).
mistakes.explain: After a number use the plural form: 'twee dozen'.

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'er' for 'of them' (Ik heb drie).
mistakes.explain: After a number, 'er' means 'of them': 'Ik heb er drie.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses a personal pronoun for things (Ik heb ze drie / Ik heb hen drie).
mistakes.explain: For things after a number use 'er', not 'ze/hen': 'Ik heb er drie.'

mistakes.pattern: Adds 'van' after the number (Ik heb er drie van).
mistakes.explain: With a number you do not need 'van': 'Ik heb er drie.'

mistakes.pattern: Adds 'niet' to 'niemand' (Niemand weet het niet).
mistakes.explain: 'Niemand' is already negative; do not add 'niet': 'Niemand weet het.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'hij' for a thing (Niemand weet hij).
mistakes.explain: Point back with 'het' (or 'dat'), not 'hij': 'Niemand weet het.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out the object (Niemand weet).
mistakes.explain: Add the object: 'Niemand weet het.'

exercises.en: There is no one at home.

exercises.context: You are moving house and your friend is helping you. He points at a big box.
exercises.task: Say that there are books in it and that you have too many of them.
examples: Er zitten boeken in. Ik heb er te veel.
Boeken. Ik heb er echt te veel.

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'is' with plural 'boeken' (Er is boeken in).
mistakes.explain: With plural 'boeken' use 'zijn/zitten': 'Er zitten boeken in.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'er' with 'too many of them' (Ik heb te veel).
mistakes.explain: After a number or quantity, 'er' means 'of them': 'Ik heb er te veel.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'veel' instead of 'te veel' for 'too many' (Ik heb er veel).
mistakes.explain: 'Too many' is 'te veel': 'Ik heb er te veel.'

mistakes.pattern: Repeats 'er' with the preposition (Er zitten boeken erin).
mistakes.explain: Use 'er...in' as a pair: 'Er zitten boeken in', not 'Er zitten boeken erin'.

exercises.context: He picks up a box and asks what to do with it.
exercises.task: Say that the box is for you, but that it is rather big.
examples: Die is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot.
Deze doos is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'Het' for the de-word 'doos' (Het is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot).
mistakes.explain: 'De doos/deze doos' is a de-word, so point back with 'die' (or 'hij'): 'Die is voor jou.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses subject 'hij' after 'voor' (voor hij).
mistakes.explain: After a preposition use 'jou' for the person you are speaking to: 'voor jou'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'het' for the box (Het is voor jou, maar het is best wel groot).
mistakes.explain: Use 'die/hij' for 'de doos': 'Die is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'maar' (Die is voor jou. Hij is best wel groot).
mistakes.explain: The task asks for a contrast: 'Die is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot.'

mistakes.pattern: Says 'wel groot' instead of 'best wel groot' for 'rather big' (maar hij is wel groot).
mistakes.explain: 'Rather big' is 'best wel groot': 'maar hij is best wel groot.'

exercises.context: He asks about the guests who are coming later.
exercises.task: Say that both your parents are coming and that some friends are coming too.
examples: Allebei mijn ouders komen, en sommige vrienden ook.
Mijn ouders komen allebei, en sommige vrienden komen ook.

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'komt' with plural 'ouders' (Allebei mijn ouders komt).
mistakes.explain: With plural 'ouders' use 'komen': 'Allebei mijn ouders komen.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'komt' with plural 'vrienden' (Sommige vrienden komt).
mistakes.explain: With plural 'vrienden' use 'komen': 'sommige vrienden komen.'

mistakes.pattern: Places 'allebei' after 'mijn' (Mijn allebei ouders komen).
mistakes.explain: Say 'allebei mijn ouders' or 'mijn ouders allebei', not 'mijn allebei ouders'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'veel' for 'some' (Veel vrienden komen ook).
mistakes.explain: 'Some' of a group is 'sommige': 'sommige vrienden'.

say.nl: Ik neem er twee mee. En deze doos?

turns.task: Say that the box is for you, but that it is rather big.

mistakes.pattern: Uses subject 'hij' after 'voor' (voor hij).

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'het' for the box (Het is voor jou, maar het is best wel groot).
mistakes.explain: Use 'die/hij' for 'de doos': 'Die is voor jou, maar hij is best wel groot.'

mistakes.pattern: Leaves out 'maar' (Die is voor jou. Hij is best wel groot).

mistakes.pattern: Says 'wel groot' instead of 'best wel groot' for 'rather big' (maar hij is wel groot).

turns.task: Say that both your parents are coming and that some friends are coming too.
examples: Allebei mijn ouders komen, en sommige vrienden ook.
Mijn ouders komen allebei, en sommige vrienden komen ook.

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'komt' with plural 'ouders' (Allebei mijn ouders komt).
mistakes.explain: With plural 'ouders' use 'komen': 'Allebei mijn ouders komen.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses singular 'komt' with plural 'vrienden' (Sommige vrienden komt).
mistakes.explain: With plural 'vrienden' use 'komen': 'sommige vrienden komen.'

mistakes.pattern: Places 'allebei' after 'mijn' (Mijn allebei ouders komen).
mistakes.explain: Say 'allebei mijn ouders' or 'mijn ouders allebei', not 'mijn allebei ouders'.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'veel' for 'some' (Veel vrienden komen ook).
mistakes.explain: 'Some' of a group is 'sommige': 'sommige vrienden'.

turns.task: Say that the lift is there, next to the stairs.
examples: Die is daar, naast de trap.
Hij is daar, naast de trap.
De lift is daar, naast de trap.

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'Het' for 'de lift' (Het is daar).
mistakes.explain: 'De lift' is a de-word, so use 'die' or 'hij': 'Die is daar.'

mistakes.pattern: Uses 'waar' for 'there' (Die is waar).
mistakes.explain: For 'there' use 'daar'; 'waar' means 'where': 'Die is daar.'

mistakes.pattern: Says 'naar de trap' for 'next to the stairs' (Die is daar, naar de trap).
mistakes.explain: 'Next to' is 'naast': 'naast de trap'.

culture.title: De of het?
culture.text: Dutch children learn de and het word by word, and many adults still mix them up now and then. If you say 'het kaas' instead of 'de kaas', every Dutch speaker will understand you and most will not even mention it. The same goes for die and dat: the wrong choice sounds slightly off, but it never blocks the conversation. So keep talking, and let the words you meet teach you the articles.

summary: de-words and plurals: deze and die. het-words: dit and dat.
Relative clauses: die for de-words and plurals, dat for het-words, verb at the end.
er means 'there', 'of them' after a number, and it fuses with prepositions: erover, ermee, ervan, erin.
Point back at a thing with die (or hij) for de-words and het for het-words.
Choosing the wrong small word is a small mistake, not a big one: keep the conversation going.
